diagram_math_checks.objects: Observed coordinates y_j=Y_x(u_j), observed-data partial sums, pairwise acceptance tests, and selected candidate index.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition paragraphs 2 and 4 specify exactly this operational order. The arrows indicate processing order, not Hilbert-space morphisms or equalities.

The Definition constructs each finite observed partial sum as sum_{j=1}^N s_j q_{alpha_m}(lambda_j)y_j v_j. Its X-limit, or 0_X on nonconvergence, is the estimator used by the tests; the diagram is schematic and does not replace that unchanged definition.

For every 0 <= m_1 < m_2 <= m_max the test is ||xhat_{m_1}(y)-xhat_{m_2}(y)||_X <= eta_{m_1,m_2}, with eta=sigma z_{m_1,m_2}(x_{m_1})+beta sqrt(v_{m_1,m_2}). All finer indices m_2 > m_1 must pass. No sign, comparison direction, quantile argument, or indexing changed.

The final node is the smallest accepted index mhat; the Definition returns alphahat=alpha_{mhat} on alpha_0>...>alpha_{m_max}. The terminal candidate m_max is accepted without comparisons, also for m_max=0. Shared sizing and downward orientation add no mathematical condition.

diagram_math_checks.independence: The item remains an algorithm without a supplied phase proof. Its properties are proved using the coordinate definitions and inequalities as the existing Rule diagram prose explicitly states; no proof relies on the illustration.
